findings.claim: DECISIVE NEGATIVE: the on-disk floor record's masked-image blob is NOT the 4-plane planar work-buffer the OR-blit reads, and is NOT obtainable by any flat re-layout of it. Proof: an exhaustive sliding-subset search (every byte-stride w=4..40, every dest byte-col 8..31, every dest row 30..143) found NO placement where the floor blob is even a BITWISE SUBSET of the OR-blit page's plane 0 (best zero-violation score = -1, i.e. no alignment is OR-compatible). Since the OR-blit only does `page |= src` (it can only ADD bits, never clear them), if the blob were the source there MUST exist a placement where blob is a bitwise subset of the page. There is none. Therefore an EXPAND/DECODE step transforms the record blob into the dense planar work-buffer before the OR-blit. This converts the prior 'masked-image' suspicion into a proof and rules out the simplest from-asset hypothesis (record blob == OR-blit source).

evidence.details: Floor = bank2 rec2 (1346B, decodeAsset). Blob starts at record +0x64 (block far-ptr +0x84): `2a 00 28 00 a8 0a 8a 02 00 00 00 a2 ...` (1246 bytes). Byte histogram: 0x00 = 724/1246 (58%), then 0x80,0xaa,0xa0,0x02,0x08,0x88,0x2a,0x8a,0xa2,0x28 (all values whose set bits cluster in ODD positions). Bit-position counts (bit0..7) = [89,232,88,233,87,241,93,247]: odd bits (1,3,5,7) ~2.7x the even bits (0,2,4,6). This sparse, mostly-zero, bit-position-biased distribution is a packed/masked encoding, not dense planar. The page floor band (y128, plane0, byte-cols 11..28) is dense: `5a b4 03 3e a0 7e 0b 2e 5f ff ff fe ...` vs the blob `2a 00 28 00 a8 0a 8a 02 ...` — no match at the documented (88,128)w18 placement nor anywhere (exhaustive subset search = no hit).

findings.claim: There is NO resident decoded work-buffer copy of the floor sub-images anywhere in guest RAM in the settled maze state. Scanning the entire low+mid RAM region (0x10000..0x90000) for the floor blob's 8-byte signature `2a 00 28 00 a8 0a 8a 02` returns EXACTLY ONE hit: 0x78474 = floorSeg(0x783f)<<4 + 0x84 = the record block itself. The work-buffer the OR-blit reads (prior-pass source segs ~0x29a3, at-store bytes `ab 23 ac ad 6d ad cd 2d`) is BUILT TRANSIENTLY at OR-blit time and is GONE once the frame settles (the source segment then holds unrelated heap data). So the record->work-buffer expansion cannot be observed from a settled state; it is only live-capturable while the OR-blit is actively running.

findings.claim: The maze-corridor background OR-blit page uses only EGA planes 0 and 3 — planes 1 and 2 are entirely zero across the whole viewport. Every page byte decodes as `XX 00 00 YY` (plane0=XX, plane1=0, plane2=0, plane3=YY). The resulting indices are exactly {0,1,8,9,10}: index 8 (plane3 only = 0x55 dark grey), 9 (planes 0+3), 1 (plane0 only), 10 (planes 1+3 — the sparse accent). This means the floor/ceiling stone is a 2-bit (effectively) image and the record blob's decode only needs to produce plane0 + plane3 rows (plane1/plane2 output are zero). This is a useful constraint on the eventual masked decoder: it emits into 2 of the 4 planes for the grey stone, and the window adds the colored accents (the committed gy=121 oracle additionally has indices 5 and 13 = the portcullis colors, which DO touch planes 1/2).

findings.claim: ega.drv DISPATCH ENTRY 9 (file 0x27 -> FUN_1c25) is a FILE-LOAD + RLE decompressor (DOS int21 lseek 0x42 / read 0x3f into a buffer, then an RLE walk: `lodsb; if 0 stop; if al<0x80: cl=al, rep movsb (literal run); else: neg al, cl=al, lodsb, rep stosb (fill run)`). This is the .pic-family graphics LOADER (the wall-atlas path), NOT the floor/ceiling masked-blob expander — floor/ceiling are loaded verbatim by the wroot bank reader (maze-asset-loader.json), so they never pass through 0x1c25. The record-blob -> planar work-buffer expand is therefore a DIFFERENT routine, most likely in wmaze (the caller that also builds the placement/descriptor tables in the cs:[0x149] data segment), invoked just before each OR-blit group. It was not pinned this pass.

evidence.details: ndisasm ega.drv 0x1c25..0x1c93: prologue reads a file (ah=0x42 lseek, ah=0x3f read cx=0x1000 into [bp+0xc]), then the classic RLE: 0x1c74 `lodsb; or al,al; jz done; test 0x80; jnz fill; mov cl,al; rep movsb` / fill: `neg al; mov cl,al; lodsb; rep stosb`. Dispatch table (file 0x00..0x46, 4-byte `call rel16; retf` thunks): entry15 (file 0x3f) -> 0xa93 (OR-blit); entry9 (0x27) -> 0x1c25 (RLE loader); entry10 (0x2b) -> 0x1c94 (wall compositor). The OR-blit (0xa93) reads its placement table cs:[0x190] and descriptor table cs:[0x18e] from the RUNTIME data segment cs:[0x149] (NOT from ega.drv's own 0x2262-byte file) -> both tables AND the source work-buffer are caller-built (wmaze), confirming ega.drv is a pure consumer.

findings.claim: The ceiling record (bank3, 1740B) begins with a 4-byte header then a table of u16 sub-image offsets (0x2b02, 0x2b0c, 0x0000, 0x2bb6, 0x2bac, 0x2b66, 0x2af8, ..., hi-bytes 0x2b/0x2c/0x2e) — values that exceed the 1740-byte record, so they are offsets into the EXPANDED work-buffer (the decompressed concatenation of floor+ceiling+window sub-images), not into the record. These line up with the OR-blit image-descriptor `srcOff` field (cs:[0x18e] {segDelta,srcOff,w,h}). So the ceiling record header IS (a packed form of) the image-descriptor srcOff list, but it indexes the POST-EXPAND buffer — confirming again that the expand (Gap A) must run before these offsets are meaningful. The floor record by contrast starts with byte[0]=count(=1) + a sub-tile palette/ramp index table (17 18 05 06 07 08 09 0a 0e 0f 10 ...) + zero padding + the masked blob at +0x64. The window/portcullis has no separate DB id; its colored sub-images live inside these same floor/ceiling records (consistent with maze-asset-loader.json).

evidence.details: Ceiling bank3 rec2 head: `00 00 00 00 | 02 2b 0c 2b 00 00 b6 2b ac 2b 00 00 66 2b f8 2a 00 00 5c 2b 87 01 00 01 20 2b 00 00 2a 2b ...` (u16 LE offset table). Floor bank2 rec2 head: `01 | 17 18 05 06 07 08 09 0a 0e 0f 10 08 09 0a ... 13 1c 1c 13 | 00*0x3c | +0x64: 2a 00 28 00 a8 0a 8a 02 ...`. Offsets 0x2b02..0x2e9a > 1740 -> they target the expanded buffer (the OR-blit source seg), matching the descriptor srcOff field.

what_would_unblock: Gap A (the make-or-break): pin the wmaze routine that EXPANDS the record blob into the 4-plane planar work-buffer (the masked-image decompressor). Approach: DOSBox-X or patched-core breakpoint on the OR-blit ENTRY (ega.drv 0xa93 at the live reloc base) DURING the dungeon first-render (state-4 -> state-5 transition, NOT a settled forward-step) — single-step back up the call stack to the caller (wmaze) that filled cs:[0x149]/cs:[0x18e]/cs:[0x190] and the source segment, and disasm the loop that writes the work-buffer from the record block (far-ptr seg 0x783f/0x7895 +0x20). The blob bit-bias (odd bits 2.7x even) + the 2-effective-plane page output are strong shape constraints for validating the decoded rows. The decode is geometry-INDEPENDENT, so cracking it once at gy=118 generalizes to gy=121.

Gap B (placement generation): RE the wmaze placement-list builder (the code that fills cs:[0x190]). Candidates: wmaze view_render_corridor_frame (0x4ad7) + the per-depth convergence arrays (DGROUP 0x42 left / 0x4a right) drive the perspective triangle; the black-void + window placements are geometry-keyed. This is the analogue of the already-cracked wall span generator (maze-span-build.json). It must be derivable statically from wmaze (the relocated copy, 0x4564 delta) without the live tables.

Tooling: bridge the patched/nightly DBPSerialize_CPU formats so the patched trace core can unserialize the committed gy=121 state (then the OR-blit is live-capturable for the exact gate frame); OR find the precise drive that re-triggers the OR-blit on the patched core (the prior 99.93% pass DID capture it at base 0x6ba10 — that drive/state was not reproducible this run).
